title: Mechanistic evolution across the C3–C4 continuum
positioning: Collaborative unpublished research led by Dr. Chilperic Armel Foko Kuate on the coupled physiology and evolutionary accessibility of C3-like, C3–C4 intermediate and C4-like phenotypes.
public_scope: Research questions, broad model classes, limitations, selected non-reconstructive outputs and attribution only. Full equations, executable research code, detailed parameterization and calibration material are not public.
scientific_question: Starting from plausible C3-like populations, which heritable biochemical, anatomical, hydraulic, thermal and resource-allocation changes generate viable and evolutionarily accessible intermediate or C4-like phenotypes under different environments?
process_layers: C3 biochemical baseline and photorespiratory constraints
mechanistically represented intermediate states along the C3–C4 continuum
progressive recruitment of carbon-concentrating traits and C4 biochemistry
temperature-dependent physiology and leaf energy balance
soil-to-leaf hydraulics including water-temperature effects on viscosity
replicated finite-population evolution with inheritance, mutation/segregation, selection and drift
interpretation_rules: Intermediate mechanisms are included when required by the biological hypothesis; C2 is one possible mechanism, not the organizing target or a forced stage.
Assimilation is a physiological performance component, not reproductive fitness by itself.
CMA-ES, NSGA-II, grids and continuation are landscape/search tools and are not biological generations.
Failed or nonphysical simulations remain explicit failures.
Measured, literature-anchored, calibrated, derived, assumed, scenario and missing quantities are distinguished.
limitations: No public figure establishes a natural evolutionary history by itself.
Species-level calibration and external validation remain incomplete.
Genetic/mutational covariance and physiology-to-reproductive-fitness mapping are major uncertainties.
Water-viscosity effects do not replace biological hydraulic resistance and vulnerability.
The public repository is intentionally insufficient to reconstruct the unpublished scientific model.
